primary_metric: chamfer_mm per scan vs paper Table 1 (mean 0.88); PSNR/SSIM from ss-eval --split test vs paper Table 3 (32.51 / 0.942, 15-scan average only -> all 15 scans)
post_train: PYTHONPATH=$HOME/models/gsurfels-pylib:$HOME/models/dtueval-pylib CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<same gpu> /home/sejain/splatify/tools/ssenv gsurfels-dtu-eval --run <run> --data <data> --dtu /home/sejain/datasets/dtu_official/gt   # writes <run>/dtu_cd.json (~2.5 min mesh + ~2.5-4.5 min CD, CPU-heavy)

control.note: same pipeline with only L_p + L_m (in-house control, not the paper's 3DGS row 2.58 mm)

dtu-gsurfels._doc: Gaussian Surfels authors' DTU (HF turandai/gaussian-surfels-dtu, IDR layout, masks + Omnidata normals). 1600x1200; test = NeuS2 split (sorted ids 8,13,16,21,26,31,34 [+56]); validation = byte copies of test; images masked on black (official PSNR protocol); gsurfels/ sidecar (masks, priors, downscaled images, init); points.npz = 1e6 random points visual-hull pruned; cameras.npz for the evaluator. Built by reproductions/gaussian-surfels/tools/prepare_dtu.py; NOT rebuildable by bench.py prepare.

notes: 15000 steps = paper/official iterations (LR/schedules hard-coded to absolute steps: keep --steps 15000). --num-gaussians 10000000 required (sidecar init applies only when all init points are kept). First use JIT-compiles the vendored rasterizer (~2-3 min, cached). ss-train must receive --data (bench.py does) so the sidecar is found. Smoke: 2000 steps (all at 1/4 res) 267 s on a busy GPU; full-res phase is slower (~2 GB peak). Expect ~20-40 min/scan + ~6 min mesh/CD.
